title: The backdoors nothing caught are the small edits
caption: Both groups of the 500 backdoored programs, as cumulative curves: the share of each group whose diff changes at most the number of lines across. A curve further left is a group of smaller edits. Dashed lines mark the two medians.
notes: The 49 programs no monitor caught change a median of 11 lines against 25 for the 451 that at least one caught. As a share of the program it is 0.6 against 1.28, so the survivors edit about half the file and the rest rewrite more than all of it.

Data quality: the split is defined at a 2% audit budget across seven monitors. Move the budget and the groups change, so this is a statement about that operating point rather than about backdoors in general.
Only 49 programs survive, so the left curve is built from few points and steps coarsely. Read the separation between the curves, not the shape of either one.

Edit size and generator are confounded here. o3-mini wrote 34% of the caught group but only 8% of the survivors, and it also writes the largest diffs, so some of this gap is which model was asked rather than how big the edit is.
Ported from the data explorer's cases-never-caught-structure view.
